newsitem.title: CANADA: Thai banker faces extradition hearing in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Thai banker faces extradition hearing in Canada.

text.p: A former Thai bank official faced an extradition proceeding in Canada on Monday nearly a year after he was arrested on charges of embezzling about $65 million.
Canadian and Thai police arrested Rakesh Saxena, former treasury adviser to the Bangkok Bank of Commerce, last July at the Whistler mountain resort near Vancouver.
An Indian citizen and former resident of Thailand, Saxena is accused of colluding with a group of Bangkok Bank of Commerce executives to embezzle about $65 million.
His lawyer had attempted to overturn his arrest warrant and put off the extradition proceeding. But those challenges failed and the British Columbia Supreme Court began hearing the case on Monday.
Lawyers involved in the matter said they expected it to last about 10 days.
Deborah Strachan, a Canadian prosecutor who is representing Thailand, began the case by laying out the charges against Saxena in Thailand.
Saxena is accused of embezzlement, maliciously misperforming his duties at the bank, violating public trust and causing bank officials to commit offences, Strachan said.
The Thai government took over the Bangkok bank a year ago after a public run on deposits sparked by news it was saddled with about $2.7 billion in bad loans.

The run was triggered by opposition party charges about the bad loans and the case took on political overtones. Since Saxena's arrest, he has been named in a second similar case along with Saudi tycoon Adnan Khashoggi.

Saxena's lawyer, Winton Derby, raised objections to much of the witness testimony presented by Thailand, saying it was hearsay. He also told the court he wanted to make clear that Saxena was reserving his right to appeal further the decision upholding the arrest warrant against him.
